item.title: Workplace wellbeing and the power of singing together
item.description: Kate Ayres’ experience of setting up a university choir showed her that staff wellbeing initiatives are most effective when they are co-produced

item.title: Why does DfE subcontract graduate statistics to the IFS?
item.description: Paul Wiltshire argues that influential reports on the graduate premium risk distorting public understanding of higher education’s financial value.

item.title: Is it a loan or a tax? It wasn’t supposed to be either
item.description: A new poll shows widespread dissatisfaction with student finance, but little agreement on the remedy. Jim Dickinson suggests the divide reflects competing mental models of the system

item.title: How Ukraine regulates AI in education during the Russian invasion
item.description: Traditional regulatory systems aren't set up to manage fast-moving technologies. Dmytro Chumachenko and Bo Kelestyn argue that Ukraine's pragmatic approach could hold lessons for others

item.title: The choices universities and colleges make about AI are political
item.description: Ahead of this week's Digifest, Michael Webb and Rebecca Flook confront the complex values systems behind general purpose AI technology

item.title: Decision-making, for regulators
item.description: The Office for Students makes many regulatory decisions, but the evidence for these decisions is often hard to come by. David Kernohan asks whether more transparency would make for better regulation

item.title: An office that bears students’ name ought to be acting in their interests
item.description: Jim Dickinson compares OfS approach to students against other UK regulators – and finds a regulator that lacks the mechanisms, the rigour, and the will to act on what students are telling it

item.title: What the government’s Social Cohesion Action Plan means for universities and students
item.description: Jim Dickinson explores how the government’s latest social cohesion plans revive longstanding tensions on campus between Prevent compliance and free speech duties

item.title: Who gets permission to enjoy their education?
item.description: From GCSEs to university, expectations around “realism” vary by background. Hannah Rolley considers what this means for widening participation and students’ freedom to choose what they study

item.title: The MRes boom isn’t just an issue of visa policy
item.description: Rumours of Home Office action on the dramatic growth in research master’s provision continue to swirl. Yet for Michael Salmon there’s a wider question about where responsibility lies for postgraduate-level study
